newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police deny Bre-X workers held hostage at Busang.
newsitem.headline: Police deny Bre-X workers held hostage at Busang.

text.p: Indonesian police on Wednesday denied that two senior employees of Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd were being held hostage by their colleagues at the Busang base camp in East Kalimantan.
"It's not true two Bre-X employees were being held hostage by other workers," Lieutenant-Colonel Iwan Ismet, head of police in the Kutai regency where Busang is located, told Reuters.
"I went there (the base camp) by helicopter yesterday and spoke to one of the employees who was allegedly held by the workers," Ismet said. "He said: 'Who is saying I am being held hostage'?"
Ismet said the 372 Bre-X employees at the camp were worried they would not get paid following the collapse of the Busang project after independent tests found virtually no gold there.
Indonesia has frozen all activites of Bre-X and its subsidiaries operating in the country until police investigations into the scandal are completed.

Bre-X had previously declared that the Busang property contained about 71 million ounces of gold, making it the biggest gold find this century. But an independent audit of the property found no significant gold deposit.

Canadian consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd also found that data pegged to the Busang discovery had been falsified on an unprecedented scale, prompting investigations by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Indonesian police.

The official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday that Bre-X's head of administration and personnel, identified only as Idris, and surveyor Agus Tripadi had reportedly been held by the workers since Sunday before a proposed lay-off.
Ismet said Idris went to the Bre-X office in Samarinda on Tuesday to inquire about the employees' wages and was told that they were likely to be paid over the next two days.
"All the workers want is to be paid their wages and lay-off compensation in accordance with Indonesian laws," he said.
Ismet said six policemen had been stationed at the camp.
